newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Nov 20.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.
-- French authorities denies breaking a UN arms embargo with an alleged 1994 arms delivery to Rwanda.

-- Air France orders 10 Boeing 777 and places options for 10 more. It also orders 10 Airbus aircraft and places options for five more. Air France is expected to post a 802-million-franc first-half profit today.

-- Rolls-Royce invites state-owned SNECMA to cooperate in aircraft engine manufacturing for the over-500-seat future Boeing and Airbus superjumbos, and for lengthened versions of Airbus long-haul A340.
-- Industry Minister Franck Borotra says Renault and Peugeot cannot rely solely on early retirements to solve competitiveness problems, calls for industrial cooperation.
-- Unions at EDF-GDF utility supplier call for strike on December 3.

-- Government is due to reshuffle Bank of France's monetary policy council as two members' mandates expire at the end of the year. The choice of new members will provide insight into the level of the government's committment to a strong currency.
-- GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud refuses to bow to government's demand that he resign, denies having blocked privatisation of subsidiary CIC.
